hypothesis: The F0.5 jump from 0.8406 to 0.9133 on the synthetic test set is an artifact of generator/evaluation coupling and/or threshold re-tuning rather than genuine pipeline generalization.
change: 4-quadrant ablation audit isolating Parser (old vs new), Generator (old vs new), and Threshold (0.20 vs 0.30).
fp_findings: 0 FPs at threshold 0.20/0.30 due to 1-to-1 bipartite lock and street number penalty.
fn_findings: Single-token brand + landmark-only address pairs with 0 token overlap.
feature_audit: tfidf_name_cosine and char3_addr_jaccard highest importance; no feature > 35%.
leakage_audit: Generator bug uncovered: s1_addr.replace('Main St', 'M. St') silently failed on French 'Rue de la Paix' addresses, giving uncorrupted exact addresses to S2 multi-matches in the new generator.
adversarial_result: Score jump was entirely falsified: caused by generator silent failure leaving identical addresses, not parser or threshold.
next_hypothesis: Fix the French address corruption in multi-match generation, then evaluate genuine impact of parser.

hypothesis: Universal country-aware address perturbation and locality corruption across S2 and S3 eliminates exact-duplicate leakage, yielding a genuine adversarial test.
change: Replaced hardcoded .replace() with corrupt_street_address + multi-match S3 locality corruption.

hypothesis: Generalized trailing number parsing without keyword gating extracts street numbers from abbreviated European streets, boosting recall without introducing false merges.
change: Replaced keyword-gated trailing regex with general trailing number regex on the street phrase and stripped number from street body.

hypothesis: Auditing and replacing rigid closed-vocabulary assumptions in acronym generation and normalization (accent stripping, dotted abbreviation collapse, international legal forms) prevents silent failure on non-ASCII/non-US corporate records.
change: Added unicodedata NFKD accent stripping, dotted initials collapse, expanded international legal forms (AG, PLC, BV, NV, SPA, SASU, CIE), and stripped legal forms before acronym initial extraction.

hypothesis: Evaluating on independent public benchmark FEBRL4 (10,000 records, 5,000 true links) with all cheat IDs (dob, ssn) stripped verifies generalizability and allows testing active hard-negative mining.
change: Loaded FEBRL4 as S1 (5k) and S2 (5k), ran multi-key blocking, 15 decomposed features, and evaluated hard-negative mining.
notes: Zero false merges on 750 held-out test entities; all 337k non-matches scored P < 0.20. Automated error taxonomy shows 73% of remaining misses are typo_heavy_name_address.

hypothesis: Evaluating on real-world public corporate restaurant/chain benchmark (Fodors-Zagat: 533 businesses, 423 singletons) tests branch conflicts, noisy addresses, and singletons on authentic enterprise records.
change: Formulated Fodors-Zagat into S1 reference vs S2 candidate tables, ran full blocking, 15 decomposed features, and collective resolution.
notes: 100.00% blocking recall, 100.00% test recall, 99.54% precision. Surfaced real-world co-located sub-venue edge case (Restaurant Ritz-Carlton Atlanta vs Ritz-Carlton Cafe at 181 Peachtree St).

hypothesis: Adding sublinear character 3-5 gram TF-IDF cosine within word boundaries (analyzer='char_wb') insulates the model against vocabulary shift and decreses reliance on word TF-IDF.
change: Integrated tfidf_char_cosine as 16th feature in extract_pairwise_features and fit char_wb vectorizer with sublinear_tf=True.
notes: Word TF-IDF dominance dropped from 25.0% to 19.2%. Character TF-IDF captured 15.1% of splits. Highest single feature is now < 20%.

hypothesis: Replacing difflib with RapidFuzz C++, transliterating Indic scripts with anyascii, expanding address/number blocking keys, and mining real blocking hard negatives directly from the inverted index eliminates the 8k false merge explosion, speeds up feature extraction by >20x, and elevates real-data generalization above 0.95 F0.5.
change: Integrated RapidFuzz (ratio, token_sort_ratio), anyascii transliteration for Indic scripts, inverted index hard negative mining (positives + 10 blocking hard negs + 2 random), precomputed sparse TF-IDF dict lookups (195x speedup), and 18 pairwise features (added full address lev alv and missing address mad).
notes: F0.5 jumped from 0.8300 baseline to 0.9509. False positives dropped from 8,276 to 534. Feature extraction on 1.33M validation pairs finished in 37.5s with zero difflib or scipy slicing bottlenecks.

hypothesis: Verifying generalization with a strict 3-way split (20k Train -> 2.5k Val for tuning -> 2.5k Held-Out Test evaluated only once at T_opt) proves zero threshold leakage, while fixing the North/Nouvelle/Nord address regex bug and adding French legal forms (EURL/SCI/SASU/SARL) ensures open-set French records match accurately.
change: Strict 3-way split (20k/2.5k/2.5k), fixed no\b address regex bug, preserved commas for address decomposition, added leetspeak digit repair, expanded French legal forms and stopwords, and evaluated synthetic French open-set test cases.
notes: Held-out test score (0.9481) perfectly matches validation score (0.9477) with zero threshold tuning leakage. French synthetic open-set stress test passed 8/8 (100.0%) with P=1.0000 on true matches.
